{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVlzVyc8AAAABi_d5rg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BqjeczhMVquI", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bqjec", "number": 30, "title": "Add configurable approval modes and LLM-based automatic action review", "body": "## Goal

Introduce flexible approval modes inspired by Codex's "Approve for me" (Guardian), while keeping Cognix's agent loop and two-tool interface simple. Allow routine development work to proceed without asking the user to approve every action, while retaining enforceable security boundaries.

## Current behavior

After #26 and #28, Cognix exposes `run_command` and `apply_patch`. Every command and patch needs manual approval; commands run in a fixed read-only macOS sandbox with no network. There is no AI reviewer or configurable approval mode.

## Proposed behavior

### Approval modes

- `manual` (default): ask the user to approve actions that require approval.
- `auto`: route actions requiring approval to a separate LLM review context; execute only if the reviewer allows the action and the enforced policy permits it. A rejection blocks the action. Uncertain, invalid, unavailable or timed-out reviews fall back to explicit user confirmation; cancellation never authorizes execution.
- `full-access`: explicitly selected, clearly warned mode without ordinary approval or sandbox restrictions. Never enter this mode automatically or as a fallback.

Keep the sandbox policy separate from the approval mechanism. Support read-only and workspace-write isolation, with workspace-write as the normal development profile, network denied by default, and access outside the permitted workspace restricted. Allow narrowly scoped additional permissions, including network access, only through an explicit approval path. Preserve optional exact-argv restrictions and hard policy denials in manual/auto modes. Unknown or potentially destructive operations require review; only narrowly defined low-risk operations may bypass approval. A command name alone does not establish safety, and tests/builds may execute arbitrary project code. Do not infer blanket permission from a failed sandboxed command or a prior approval.

### Reviewer configuration

Use the existing Ollama provider and the same model by default, with an independent reviewer conversation and security prompt. Allow the user to select a different locally available model in `~/.cognix/config.toml`:

```toml
model = "qwen3.8:27b"
review_model = "qwen3.8:27b"
approval_mode = "auto"
sandbox_mode = "workspace-write"
```

When `review_model` is omitted, use the effective working model (including CLI overrides). Keep existing config precedence, local-only inference restrictions and launcher behavior. Ensure reviewer compatibility/model availability is handled explicitly; the reviewer must not need tool-calling support. Do not require separate model training.

### Review request and verdict

Review the exact prepared action before execution. Pass a dedicated security instruction and structured evidence, including:

- Original user instructions and relevant conversation history, including prior explicit approvals/denials; distinguish trusted user authorization from assistant claims and untrusted tool output.
- The selected tool's description, validated arguments and expected side effects.
- For commands: exact argv, resolved executable, working directory and applicable execution restrictions.
- For patches: target path, actual proposed change/diff and relevant pre-edit state.
- Effective sandbox/permissions, requested additional permissions, and reason for approval when applicable.

Use a bounded review context. The reviewer has no tool execution authority and cannot grant permissions beyond the enforced policy. Its structured response contains `decision` (`allow`, `deny`, or `ask_user`) and `reason`. Validate the response strictly; never treat arbitrary text as approval. Bind approval to the exact reviewed action and effective permissions, revalidate before execution, and do not silently retry a denial using an equivalent action.

Keep the existing command/patch execution and agent loop; add the reviewer at the approval boundary. Do not build a general multi-agent framework or reproduce Codex's entire permission system.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Configuration supports manual/auto/full-access approval modes and a separate reviewer model; default model inheritance and config validation work.
- [ ] In auto mode, the reviewer receives the actual proposed command or patch and relevant authorization context in an independent inference request. Approved actions execute only within the applicable sandbox/policy; denied actions do not execute.
- [ ] Uncertain or malformed responses, reviewer errors and timeouts require manual confirmation or safely stop if confirmation is unavailable; cancellation stops execution. Hard denials cannot be overridden by AI approval.
- [ ] Workspace-write supports ordinary project-local build/test workflows while restricting outside writes and network by default; additional permissions are explicit and scoped. Full access requires deliberate opt-in and is never a fallback.
- [ ] Tests cover safe inspection, legitimate edits/tests, destructive commands unrelated to user intent, network restrictions, prompt injection in tool output, invalid verdicts, exact-action binding and manual fallback. Verify actual sandbox enforcement on macOS; do not rely on model output alone.
- [ ] Run a small real Ollama evaluation of both normal development tasks and unsafe/ambiguous proposals. Record review decisions, false approvals/denials and latency; do not claim perfect safety.
- [ ] Update README with configuration examples, mode behavior, permissions and limitations.

## References

- [Codex Guardian review request data](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/ext/guardian-reviewer/src/approval_request.rs)
- [Codex Guardian prompt construction](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/guardian/prompt.rs)
- [Codex reviewer model selection](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/core/src/guardian/reviewer_config.rs)
